title: Authentic Audience
before:
In interdisciplinary learning, it is important for students to see their work in the world around them. Whether that is at the level of the classroom, town, state, or beyond, it helps students share their learning and receive feedback from their communities. These opportunities also allow for community involvement, which is a keystone of the Maine school experience.

Authentic Audience

Authentic audiences are a key part of interdisciplinary instruction since they give students a purpose for their work. This short video gives actionable tips for developing authentic audiences.

Resources

  • Creating Authentic Audiences for Student Work — Low to high-prep ways to incorporate an authentic audience in the classroom.
  • Sharing Student Work Beyond the Classroom — The Share Your Learning Campaign and ideas for including an authentic audience.
  • How to Prepare Students for Explaining their Work in Public — Ideas for preparing students to share their learning with an authentic audience.

decisions.label: Drop the dash once the link is set apart
decisions.why: 3 of those items separate the link from its description with a dash. The link is now set in the display face at a larger size with a chevron after it, so the dash marks a boundary that is already unmistakable. Only the separator is removed — no word changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 3 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
